hook: The Pacific Ocean is hitting record-breaking temperatures, hotter than any point in recorded history.

sections.voiceover: The Pacific Ocean is hitting record-breaking temperatures, hotter than any point in recorded history.
sections.visual_cue: Satellite imagery showing thermal anomalies in the central Pacific Ocean.
sections.sfx_cue: Distant sound of crashing waves building in intensity.
b_roll: NASA Earth Observatory satellite global sea surface temperature map

sections.voiceover: In October 2026, the Bureau of Meteorology confirmed record-breaking sea-surface temperatures across the central Pacific. How is this heat impacting California?
sections.visual_cue: Animated timeline comparing 1997, 2015, and 2026 temperature markers.
sections.sfx_cue: Low frequency hum that pulses with the dates.
b_roll: Bureau of Meteorology sea surface temperature chart

sections.voiceover: This heat is driving unprecedented king tide flooding across Southern California coastal communities.
sections.visual_cue: Wide shot of high water levels encroaching on coastal infrastructure.
sections.sfx_cue: Sound of rushing water and urban traffic noise.
b_roll: Footage of Newport Beach business district flooding

sections.voiceover: King tides will rise another one to two feet in Orange County coastal neighborhoods.
sections.visual_cue: Map showing the Pacific Coast Highway with flood hazard zones highlighted.
sections.sfx_cue: Sound of sirens in the distance.

sections.voiceover: Bureau of Meteorology data confirms this 2026 event is the hottest on record.
sections.visual_cue: Slow zoom out from a calm but rising shoreline.
sections.sfx_cue: Sound of ocean waves fading out.
